newsitem.title: KENYA: Two killed, stalls set ablaze on Kenya's coast.
newsitem.headline: Two killed, stalls set ablaze on Kenya's coast.

text.p: Two people were killed on Kenya's coast early on Tuesday and fire destroyed more than 300 curio stalls in a resort as a week of violence hit a tourist site for the first time.

The destruction of the stalls was also the first time unrest reached as far as Malindi, 120 km (75 miles) north of Mombasa city, the centre of attacks and violence in which at least 37 people have been killed since last Wednesday.
On the Malindi beachfront, stall-holders from tribal areas deep in Kenya wept as they sifted through the charred remains of an estimated 375 stalls, salvaging some blackened trinkets.
"Someone saw people came with a jerrycan of petrol which they sprayed on the kiosks before lighting them," stall-holder David Kenyakenga told Reuters. "We had not received any direct threats here."
"This was the start of the high season and what we make now helps us through the hard times later," said Joyce Atima, picking up stone chess pieces from what was left of her stall.
"I am going back to my land in Kisii (in western Kenya). I have no other choice," she said before bursting into tears.
Residents said the blaze began at about midnight but no one was hurt. They said the site was owned by the town council, which wanted the stall-owners to move so it could be sold to a developer.
Most civilian casualties since last Wednesday were Kenyans from outside the Indian Ocean coastal region. Hand-written pamphlets have called for them to be driven out by natives.
Hassan Haji, deputy commissioner of the coast province, said police believed the arson was "a criminal act" by people taking advantage of the violence around Kenya's second city Mombasa.
No tourists have been injured in the unrest, but foreigners have been told by their governments to avoid troublespots. The United States has warned Americans against going to the coast.
Malindi is a centre for tourists and expatriates from Italy who own homes and businesses such as restaurants in the area.

In Mombasa, Haji said 150 people armed with bows and arrows and G-3 and AK-47 assault rifles attacked a seven-man police patrol in Mtwapa just north of the Indian Ocean port city early on Tuesday. In an exchange of fire police shot dead one person.

He also said early on Tuesday vigilantes killed a man in Kitaruni, nine km (six miles) north of Mombasa, when he tried to torch a house. Five people were slashed with machetes at Ntopanga when thugs burned three homes and attacked residents.
Tuesday's deaths brought the toll in seven days of violence in the coastal region to at least 37 dead. Haji said 189 people had been arrested so far and 42 had been charged in court.

In the capital Nairobi, President Daniel arap Moi on Tuesday warned Kenyans against tribalism, saying the country had been "pushed to the wall" repeatedly but Kenyans knew it was unlike Rwanda and Burundi which were destroyed by ethnic hatred.
Moi's government and the opposition, heading for elections later this year which threaten to bring more trouble, have blamed each other for the string of brutal attacks on the coast.
Police said they had recovered 12 stolen rifles but 38 were still missing with ammunition and appealed to the public.
Haji said anything that threatened tourism was a threat to most Kenyans. The industry is the country's top employer and foreign currency earner, bringing in $465 million in 1996.
Tourist officials meanwhile said cancellations were picking up. An official with the firm Abercrombie and Kent said they had received 56 cancellations for coast holidays so far this week.
Several political activists are among those arrested in a hunt by police, the army and the navy for the attackers.

Haji said Emmanuel Maitha, an official with Moi's ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party, was in custody and being questioned. He would be charged if he was found to have been involved in the well-organised coastal violence, Haji added.
